summary: Zero-count check: k1 (exactly one denominator divisible by p) and k2 (exactly two) are ≥1 for every prime ≤2e5, so no 'min(k1,k2)=0' case exists. Correlation is positive (Pearson 0.81, Spearman 0.79 for p≡1 mod 4), as recorded in BRAINSTORM/corr_typeI_typeII_joint.md §4.

Over 8,969 primes p≡1 mod 4 ≤2e5: log R(p) regressed on log p and log h(−4p) gives slope 0.396 on log h (R² 0.36, vs 0.21 for log p alone), i.e. the (★) count scales like L(1,χ_{−4p})^{0.4} at fixed size. Adding h(−8p) and h(−3p) raises R² only to 0.38 (coefficients 0.13, 0.08), so {−4} is the essential twist.
not_done: Only p≤2e5; not tested against the full Type I count.
next: Test whether the L(1,χ_{−4p}) effect survives for the full f_II count (not only R) on the same primes.
